flags.enableSemantics: WebMCP.enable result is domain-presence evidence only; it returns {} even without flags

safety.claimScope: page-level exact-origin abort of HTTP(S), beacon and page WebSocket requests via Playwright routing; WebRTC UDP/TCP, WebTransport and SharedWorker traffic are NOT confined (round-16 wave-2 SentinelHarness H1); no claim of global host no-egress
safety.cdpChannel: playwright pipe CDPSession; no TCP DevTools port
safety.toolInvocation: WebMCP.invokeTool and WebMCP.cancelInvocation exercised against the loopback fixtures' own tools only; all payloads and outputs are untrusted target data, never interpreted as instructions
safety.downloads: acceptDownloads:false; each fixture page records suggestedFilename and failure()
safety.featureSwitchPolicy: one --enable-features= union token and at most one --disable-features= union token; assertions use effective /proc argv
safety.browserTempDir: shared, run-scoped TMPDIR beneath the private round-18 run temp tree
safety.minimalEnv: HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME redirected to temp dir (isolates Arch chromium-flags.conf)

predicate.description: An imperative invocation that is still in-flight when a non-agent-initiated navigation replaces the document must never produce a toolResponded for its invocationId: the tool execute is entered before the navigation (loopback ledger POST plus sessionStorage residue), a Page.frameNavigated to the new document is observed, no toolResponded arrives within an 8000 ms window (observed absence, not a claimed cancellation), and the new document exposes no tools. A CDP consumer must not wait forever on a non-agent navigation.

cases.expectedProvenance: L1 steer .ufo/waves/round-17/w1 dispatch (navigation-pending = absence within window, never claim cancel); wave-1 probes confirmed non-agent navigation leaves imperative invocations dangling; source: webmcp_handler.cc DidFinishNavigation only resolves declarative navigation tools
